item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Pakistan’s Shuttle Diplomacy Unfolds in Tehran
item.summary: Pakistan’s foreign ministry said it expected to host a second round of U.S.-Iran talks but did not say when, as a Pakistani delegation visited the Iranian capital.

item.title: Russian Strikes Kill at Least 15 in Ukraine in Biggest Attack in Months
item.summary: Moscow is again ramping up missile and drone attacks on civilian targets, dispelling any notion that a temporary cease-fire for Orthodox Easter might become more lasting.

item.title: Dodging Bombs and Drones, This Postman in Ukraine Still Delivers
item.summary: Oleksiy Klochkovsky has driven mail and parcels around the front line in Ukraine for four years. He keeps one ear tuned for danger from above.

item.title: Top U.S. Diplomat in Venezuela Leaves Post After Arriving in January
item.summary: Laura Dogu, who reopened the U.S. Embassy in Venezuela, returns to advising Gen. Dan Caine, the highest ranking U.S. military officer, as the war with Iran continues.

item.title: With Iran War on Pause, Political Battle Resumes Over Israeli Democracy
item.summary: A court fight over Itamar Ben-Gvir, an extremist who oversees the police, pits the attorney general against Benjamin Netanyahu and his right-wing government.

item.title: Trump Says Leaders From Israel and Lebanon Will Speak Thursday
item.summary: Neither side confirmed a meeting. Israeli and Lebanese officials have said a cease-fire in the war against Hezbollah is under consideration.

item.title: 3 Killed in Boat Strike in the Pacific, Pentagon Says
item.summary: It was the third such attack by the U.S. military in three days, and the 51st attack in a campaign against people who the United States has accused of smuggling drugs.

item.title: Got $100 Million? Ukraine Has Just the Fertilizer Plant for You.
item.summary: An effort to privatize the facility is a key test of whether Kyiv can overcome concerns about Russian attacks and corruption to attract foreign investment.

item.title: How China’s Weapons Transfers to Iran Have Evolved Over Decades
item.summary: China has denied claims this month by U.S. intelligence that it might have shipped arms to Iran. In recent years, China has supported Iran with dual-use parts.

item.title: Claudia Sheinbaum’s War on Crime in Mexico Faces a Grim Reckoning: 133,000 Missing People
item.summary: President Claudia Sheinbaum of Mexico is under pressure to end one of her country’s most painful tragedies: the disappearance of more than 133,000 people.
